big_idea: Small potential, success pursued in isolation, is capped. Big potential is unlocked by deliberately building the people and ecosystem around you, since achievement, happiness, and well-being rise together only through connection, not competition.

tool.label: The SEEDS framework
tool.text: Five practices for growing big potential: Surround yourself with positive, complementary people; Expand your power by giving it away; Enhance others through genuine praise; Defend your team against negativity; and Sustain gains through a virtuous cycle of reinforcement.
tool.note: Illustrated with case studies like Kaiser Permanente's program empowering front-line receptionists to flag cancer-screening gaps, which reportedly helped save hundreds of lives.

ideas.title: Small potential has a ceiling
ideas.text: Chasing individual achievement alone caps how high you can rise, since you're limited to your own resources and energy.

ideas.title: Assists beat scoring
ideas.text: Research Achor cites found basketball assists predict team wins more reliably than individual point totals: collaboration outperforms solo effort.

ideas.title: Leadership from any seat
ideas.text: You don't need a title to expand influence; empowering people below or beside you multiplies impact more than hoarding authority.

ideas.title: Praise redirected builds trust
ideas.text: Crediting the team, and even competitors, rather than self-promoting, is shown in one case to be what actually won a partnership.

ideas.title: Cognitive diversity wins
ideas.text: Teams that combine different thinking styles consistently outperform more homogeneous expert teams.

ideas.title: Motivation fades without reinforcement
ideas.text: A single burst of inspiration dissipates fast unless you build a support system that sustains it.

try_it: Identify one energy-draining relationship or habit this week and consciously limit exposure to it.
Give one piece of specific, public credit to a teammate or collaborator instead of claiming an individual win.
Hand off one small piece of ownership or decision-making to someone else on your team this week.
After learning something useful, teach or share it with one other person within 48 hours to lock in the gain.
best_for: People whose growth feels capped by going it alone
less_useful: Readers wanting rigorous, citation-heavy research; it leans on illustrative anecdotes
Readers looking for individual-only habit or productivity advice rather than a team lens

related.why: The same author's earlier book on the research behind positivity and performance
A complementary take on unlocking potential through character and systems
